intro: A vision transformer starts with a sequence of image patches. The order of pixels, channels and patches determines what each learned projection receives.
task: Split channel-first images into non-overlapping square patches, flatten each patch in a specified order, and apply a supplied affine projection to obtain image tokens.
requirements: images has nonempty shape (B,C,H,W). patch_size is a positive integer excluding booleans; H and W must both be divisible by it.
Order patches by image row, then column. Within each patch, flatten channel first, then patch row, then patch column.

weight has shape (embedding_dim,C*patch_size**2) and bias is (embedding_dim,), with embedding_dim positive. Return flattened_patches@weight.T+bias with shape (B,(H/patch_size)*(W/patch_size),embedding_dim).
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Expose the patch-grid axes
hints.body: Reshape the image into batch, channel, grid-row, patch-row, grid-column, patch-column axes.

hints.title: Move grid axes before channel
hints.body: Before flattening each patch, place grid-row and grid-column immediately after batch, followed by channel and the two within-patch axes.

explanation: Patch extraction changes layout; the learned projection then changes feature dimension. Keeping these operations conceptually separate makes ordering errors easier to spot.
A projection whose weight is an identity matrix exposes the extracted pixel order directly. This is useful when a plausible output shape hides a transposition error.
Adapted the upstream reshape/permute and affine projection to supplied NumPy weights. Rectangular images are supported; parameter initialization and autograd are omitted.
